analysis.title: Global Markets Vol Weekly - 27th October 2026
key_insights: Recent AI sentiment reversal drove rotations vs Oct 5: US Tech (XLK) -7.3%, Semis (SMH) -14.6%, Memory stocks (UBXXMEMO) -25%, while Staples/HealthCare/Utilities (XLP/XLV/XLU) are all 6-9% higher. The S&P 500 is less than 2% from all-time highs, while Korea's Kospi2 is 40% below its summer highs.

Desk suggests defensive rebound exposure via call-spreads on laggard sectors/regions into year-end, with implied vols off their lows. Cited call-spreads: XLI 18Dec26 $175/185 (4.4x potential net payout), SX7E 18Dec26 EUR300/320, UBXEFREX 18Dec26 102.5/112.5%, KOSPI2 10Dec26 W1025/1125.

A 2m 25-delta call screen for rebound trades ranks highest payouts on EWZ (+7.65x), KWEB (+7.61x), ASHR (+5.61x), CAC (+5.50x) and KOSPI2 (+5.10x), with China/Korea, France/CAC, European Banks and Utilities at the top.

Risks that could drive further downside: broader AI credit issues (funding issues remain), degrossing (net exposure has come down but not gross) and a re-escalation of Iran tensions (potentially after the midterms).

Equity put convexity is harder to find with spot lower and vols higher. Taiwan (TWSE) and Switzerland (SMI) stand out, SMI having benefited from rotation flows into Pharma. Hedge ideas: FTSE Taiwan RIC Capped 16Dec 93% put at 2.32%, SMI 18Dec 13800 put at 115 (79bp).
FX hedge: USDCNH 1y 1.0% OTMS call digital indicative offer at 8.45%. USDCNH calls (0.13% premium, 53.4x payout on a move back to 1y lows) are more compelling than KRW because of their low premium.

Rates hedge: USD 2m5y 4.25-3.9 receiver spread offered at 25c, 5.1x max net payout on a move back to start-July levels. Desk says US back-end rates calls remain a good portfolio hedge, though an Iran-war oil spike would not necessarily rally rates.

Short-dated CSI 300 upside screens unusually attractive. The 3m NTR outperformance swap rate has risen toward the CSI 500 level and the CSI 300 futures-spot basis is at a YTD low, near the extremes of April 2025 'Liberation Day'. Buy CSI 300 Proxy Index (UBC300PR) 15Jan27 103-115% call spread for 1.8%, 5.7x max net payout, vs ASHR 15Jan27 103-115% at 2.2%.

China national-team proxy: broad A-share index ETF net inflows for 19-23 Oct 2026 were CNY 102bn (USD 15bn), the strongest week since 2024 and above the mid-July peak and the 'Liberation Day' week. CSI 300 took 31% and ChiNext 28% of inflows, with buying strong Thursday and Friday.

Japan banks (TPNBNK) have sold off ~12% on lower yields, positioning unwind and AI funding concerns. UBS Research sees 3 more BoJ hikes to June (rate to 2%), about 20bps above market pricing, and expects upward earnings revisions over November results. Desk prefers call-spreads as the near-term expression.

TPNBNK trade: buy 8Jan27 110-122% call spread at 2.22%, 4.4x max net payout if spot is at or above 830 at expiry (6% above Sep highs). Zero-cost variant: fund by selling the 90.35% put vs 756.61 spot, which means a 21.5% total sell-off from the Sep highs before losses begin.

Asia FX divergence: KRW and CNH have been resilient since July, while TWD and SGD weakened. UBS Asia Macro Strategist Rohit Arora sees continued CNH and KRW strength. The PBOC is allowing appreciation, and KRW is helped by unwound FX hedges and corporate repatriation. SGD is pressured by rate differentials vs the US at 20-year lows, and TWD by equity outflows.

Asia FX structures: 2m dual digit [USDKRW<2% OTMS, USDTWD>0.5% OTMS] at 9.85%, dual digit [USDCNH<0.7% OTMS, USDSGD>0.3% OTMS] at 9.25%, triple digit [USDCNH<0.5% OTMS, USDKRW<1.5% OTMS, USDSGD>0.5% ITMS] at 6.65% (14x potential net payout). Samsung and Hynix earnings this week could bring buybacks that fuel KRW repatriation.

SX5E's 10% single-stock weight cap has added about 4pts YTD to dividend valuations (DEDZ7 3.8pt, DEDZ8 3.9pt, DEDZ9 4.3pt). ASML is up 56% YTD vs the index up 6%, and pays a 1.1% dividend yield vs 3.7% for the rest, so capping ASML raises index dividend expectations.

UBS Investment Research sees +67.4% upside for ASML (EUR2400 TP) vs +21.5% for the rest of the index. If achieved immediately, ASML would reach 13.2% of the index and the cap would add 7.7pts to DEDZ8 and 8.4pts to DEDZ9. Trades: DEDZ9 220/240 call-spread at 4.2 (vs 190f ref), 3.8x net return on premium if DEDZ9 repeats its T12M return, and a DEDZ9>225 / SX5E<7280 dual-digital for 12.5%, 7x net convexity.

SPX options flow: investors traded 40% more delta than the futures market last week and were strongly counter-trend, with 'effective gamma' of about +$11bn on Wed/Thu/Fri, larger than the risk managed by market makers most of the week. SPX 0DTE ADV was $2.7tn (91st percentile of the past year).

vol_and_positioning: Implied vols are off their lows. Japan Banks implied vol is elevated vs history but not necessarily expensive relative to recent moves (up 45% between Mar and Sep vs a 23% option-implied move).
Dividend implied vol (DEDZ 2y ATM) has risen vs its summer lows but remains towards the bottom end of its post-COVID range.
FX vols are low but spot has been range-bound over the past year. 2m ATMF implied vols: USDCNH 1.6%, USDKRW 10.2%, USDJPY 8.0%, EURUSD 6.6%.
2m ATMF implied vols: KOSPI2 44.6% (89th percentile), EWY 47.3%, SPX 14.3%, NDX 21.8%, TWSE 27.2%, SMI 13.5%.
CSI 300 3m offshore ATM implied vol is lower, and the 3m NTR outperformance swap rate approaches that of CSI 500, which signals hedging demand. CSI 300 futures-spot basis is at a YTD low.
Degrossing: net exposure has come down but gross has not.

SPX options last week: 0DTE ADV $2.7tn (91st percentile), non-0DTE $1.4tn (66th), SPY 0DTE $675bn (85th), E-mini futures $712bn (83rd). Put/call 1.07x for SPX 0DTE and 1.52x for non-0DTE. Busiest session was Thursday 22nd.

Japan banks positioning has reset a lot lower recently, but falling yields combined with further positioning pressure remains a risk. Drawdowns since 2024 have been 17-28%, so the current ~12% sell-off is shallow.

tension_points.bear_case: Broader AI credit issues, degrossing (gross has not come down) and Iran re-escalation after the midterms can drive further downside. Keith Parker flags rising odds of both a correlated rally and selloff.
